title: Shock-induced HCNH<SUP>+</SUP> abundance enhancement in the heart of the starburst galaxy NGC 253 unveiled by ALCHEMI
question: What are the physical conditions and HCNH+ abundances in the CMZ of NGC 253 from multiple HCNH+ transitions, and what chemistry explains the abundances?

data.sensitivity: rms about 4–20 mK at 10 km/s channel width

what.value: Beam-averaged H2 column densities (1.6" beam) for each GMC

evidence.quote: we directly utilized values for $N_{\rm H_{2}}$ from the low-density hierarchical Bayesian analysis of the ALCHEMI data at a circular beam of 1$''$6 (cite: 2024ApJ...961...18T)

what.value: Spectroscopic data for HCNH+ from CDMS

evidence.quote: The spectroscopic information was taken from the entry in the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (cite: 2016JMoSp.327...95E)

what.value: HCNH+ HCN-HCN and HCN-H2O binding energies from experiments

evidence.quote: we adopted HCN–HCN and HCN-H$_{2}$O binding energies of $E_{\rm D}=3207\pm 197$ K and $E_{\rm D}=4192\pm 68$ K

recipe.method: Extract continuum-subtracted cubes, convert to brightness temperature (Rayleigh-Jeans), build 3σ 26-connected mask from HCNH+ (2–1), apply to all transitions
Single-component Gaussian fit to HCNH+ spectra of GMCs
assumptions: Optically thin (tau<0.1; <0.3 with dilution 0.1) assuming Tex=15 K

recipe.method: Rotational diagram with linear fits; Monte Carlo with 10,000 realizations for uncertainties; abundances using N(H2) from Tanaka et al.
Coupled states approximation with MOLSCAT using the 4D PES of Bop & Lique 2023, for p-H2 and o-H2 up to 500 K; compared with CC data via WMEF
key_parameters: 30 lowest levels of HCNH+, j1 = 0–48; H2 j2=0–2 (p) and 1–3 (o); total energies up to 3500/3620 cm-1

recipe.method: RADEX (LVG) models fit to integrated intensities with emcee; uniform priors on TK, nH2, N(HCNH+)
key_parameters: Priors: TK 50–500 K, nH2 10^2–10^7 cm-3, N 10^13–10^17 cm-2; 20 walkers, 4500 steps after burn-in
assumptions: OPR 0.25, beam dilution factor unity, same emitting region for all transitions, line width averaged over transitions

recipe.method: Chempl static and PDR models; UCLCHEM two-phase C-type shock models, varying T, density, Av, G0, zeta, shock velocity
key_parameters: PDR fiducial T=500 K, n=10^3 cm-3; shock preshock density 10^3 cm-3
assumptions: Dust temperature equal to gas temperature in static models

evidence.quote: with a radial extent of $\sim$300 pc in the CMZ
The derived rotational temperatures are in the range of 12–21 K
The beam-averaged HCNH$^+$ column densities of $(0.3-1.2) \times 10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$
the HCNH$^+$ abundances are revised to (1.8–9.4)$\times 10^{-9}$ in the CMZ of NGC 253
H$_2$ number densities of $\sim 10^{2.80}-10^{3.55}$ cm$^{-3}$ with typical errors of $\sim$0.2 dex

not_stated_but_needed: Exact ALCHEMI cube versions and file names, and channel velocity resolution used
Mask expansion sizes in spatial and spectral dimensions
Spectral extraction apertures for the GMC spectra
MCMC prior on line width and how line widths/integrated-intensity ratios enter the likelihood; RADEX background temperature
Chempl/UCLCHEM input parameter grids and run times
Velocity ranges for Gaussian fit windows
missing_for_reproduction: N(H2) values require Tanaka et al. table
score_reason: Public data and many parameters given, with codes mostly public, but model inputs and mask details are incomplete.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric tables of fitted parameters and abundances, recipe mostly specified.
